provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Sorting and matching
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to group objects by colour
The pupils should be able to match objects one to one
Introduction:
We sorted things last week. Today we learn to sort and match.
Content:
Sorting means putting things together. Group red balls together. Group blue pencils together. Matching means pairing things. Give one pupil a ball. Give another pupil a ball. They match. Use Nigerian fruits. Group oranges together. Group mangoes together.
Class activity:
Give pupils coloured paper. Ask them to sort by colour. Give each pupil one bottle top. They find a partner with the same bottle top.
Evaluation questions:
Name one colour you can sort. What is matching? Show me how to match two books. Can you sort these pencils?
Summary:
Sorting puts things together. Matching pairs things.

topics.title: Numbers 1 and 2
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count and write 1 and 2
The pupils should be able to count real objects to 2
Introduction:
We can count things. Today we learn numbers 1 and 2.
Content:
Number one means one thing. Show one finger. Write number 1. Number two means two things. Show two fingers. Write number 2. Count one mango. Count two mangoes. Use naira coins. One naira coin. Two naira coins.
Class activity:
Give pupils stones. They count one stone. They count two stones. They write 1 and 2 on the board.
Evaluation questions:
How many eyes do you have? Write number 2. Show me one finger. Count two pencils.
Summary:
Number one is one thing. Number two is two things.

topics.title: Numbers 3 and 4
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count and write 3 and 4
The pupils should be able to count real objects to 4
Introduction:
We know numbers 1 and 2. Today we learn 3 and 4.
Content:
Number three means three things. Show three fingers. Write number 3. Number four means four things. Show four fingers. Write number 4. Count three books. Count four books. Use local chalks. Three chalks. Four chalks.
Class activity:
Give pupils bottle tops. They count three bottle tops. They count four bottle tops. They write 3 and 4 in sand.
Evaluation questions:
Write number 3. How many legs does a chicken have? Count four oranges. Show me four fingers.
Summary:
Number three is three things. Number four is four things.

topics.title: Number 5
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count and write 5
The pupils should be able to count five fingers
Introduction:
We know numbers up to 4. Today we learn number 5.
Content:
Number five means five things. Show five fingers. Write number 5. Count five pencils. Count five friends. Use yam tubers. One yam, two yam, three yam, four yam, five yam.
Class activity:
Pupils count their fingers. One, two, three, four, five. They write number 5 on the board with chalk.
Evaluation questions:
How many fingers do you have? Write number 5. Count five stones. Show me five fingers.
Summary:
Number five is five things. We count with our fingers.

topics.title: Numbers 6 and 7
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count and write 6 and 7
The pupils should be able to fill gaps in number sequences
Introduction:
We know numbers up to 5. Today we learn 6 and 7.
Content:
Number six means six things. Show six fingers. Write number 6. Number seven means seven things. Show seven fingers. Write number 7. Count six balls. Count seven books. Fill gaps: 1,2,3,_,5,6,_.
Class activity:
Give pupils number cards. They arrange 1 to 7. They fill gaps in sequences on the board.
Evaluation questions:
Write number 6. What comes after 5? Count seven bottle tops. Fill the gap: 4,5,_,7.
Summary:
Number six is six things. Number seven is seven things.

topics.title: Numbers 8 and 9
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count and write 8 and 9
The pupils should be able to fill gaps in number sequences
Introduction:
We know numbers up to 7. Today we learn 8 and 9.
Content:
Number eight means eight things. Show eight fingers. Write number 8. Number nine means nine things. Show nine fingers. Write number 9. Count eight pencils. Count nine books. Fill gaps: 5,6,7,_,_,10.
Class activity:
Pupils count beans from 1 to 9. They write 8 and 9 on the ground with sticks.
Evaluation questions:
Write number 9. What comes after 7? Count eight stones. Fill the gap: 6,_,8,9.
Summary:
Number eight is eight things. Number nine is nine things.

topics.title: Number 10
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count and write 10
The pupils should be able to count ten bottle tops
Introduction:
We know numbers up to 9. Today we learn number 10.
Content:
Number ten means ten things. Show ten fingers. Write number 10. Count ten bottle tops. Count ten friends. Use kola nuts. One kola, two kola, up to ten kola.
Class activity:
Pupils count ten bottle tops. They arrange ten bottle tops in a line. They write number 10 on the board.
Evaluation questions:
Write number 10. Count ten fingers. How many bottle tops do you have? Show me ten fingers.
Summary:
Number ten is ten things. We count to ten with our fingers.

topics.title: Shapes: circle and triangle
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name and draw circle and triangle
The pupils should be able to find shapes at home
Introduction:
We see shapes everywhere. Today we learn circle and triangle.
Content:
A circle is round. Like a wheel or a plate. Draw a circle. A triangle has three sides. Like a slice of yam. Draw a triangle. Find circles at home. Plates are circles. Find triangles at home. Roof shapes are triangles.
Class activity:
Pupils draw circles and triangles with chalk. They find shapes in the classroom. Clock is a circle. Ruler is a rectangle.
Evaluation questions:
Name a round shape. Draw a triangle. What shape is a plate? How many sides has a triangle?
Summary:
A circle is round. A triangle has three sides.

topics.title: Simple patterns
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to copy and continue patterns
The pupils should be able to make patterns with beads and colours
Introduction:
We see patterns in clothes. Today we learn patterns.
Content:
A pattern repeats. Red, blue, red, blue. Copy this pattern. Continue it. Use beads. Make a pattern with beads. Red bead, blue bead, red bead. Use colours. Colour pattern: yellow, green, yellow, green.
Class activity:
Pupils make patterns with coloured paper. They arrange beads in patterns. They say patterns aloud.
Evaluation questions:
What comes next in red, blue, red? Make a pattern with blocks. What colour comes after yellow in your pattern?
Summary:
Patterns repeat. We make patterns with colours and shapes.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall term work
The pupils should be able to answer quiz questions
Introduction:
We learned many things this term. Let's revise and play a game.
Content:
Count numbers from 1 to 10. Write numbers. Sort by colour. Match objects. Name shapes. Make patterns. Be ready for questions.
Class activity:
Class quiz. Teacher asks questions. Pupils raise hands. Winners get small prizes. Stars or sweets.
Evaluation questions:
Count to five. What shape has three sides? Make a pattern. What number comes after 7?
Summary:
We learned much this term. Well done everyone!
